rounds.text: Bacil Pharma Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value of Rs 24 per share, providing investors with a margin of safety of 21.7% [E23, E24]. The company’s financial health is underpinned by high-quality earnings, as evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of 1.10x, meaning reported profits are fully backed by actual cash flow [E18]. This operational strength is further highlighted by Rs 1.71 Cr in both operating and free cash flow generated in March 2026 [E19, E20]. While the stock has faced recent volatility, its compounded share price growth over the last three and five years remains robust at 30% and 18% respectively [E13, E14]. Furthermore, the company trades at a price-to-book ratio of 1.09x, which is significantly more attractive than the sector benchmark of 2.82x [E2, E7]. Conceded: E4, E6, E10, E11, E15, E21, and E30.

The bull’s reliance on a DCF-derived margin of safety [E23, E24] is undermined by the company’s abysmal capital efficiency, as the ROCE of 0.7% is vastly inferior to the sector benchmark of 11.77% [E10]. While the bull highlights cash conversion [E18, E19, E20], this metric is overshadowed by an EV/EBITDA ratio of 157.65x, which suggests the market is pricing the company at an extreme premium relative to its actual earnings power compared to the sector benchmark of 15.61x [E11]. The bull cites historical share price growth [E13, E14], but ignores the reality that the stock has cratered by 52% over the last year [E15] and currently languishes at only 17% of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: [E2, E7, E18, E19, E20]. The bull’s focus on book value [E2] fails to account for the fact that the stock is trading at a P/E of 45.41x, significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 31.01x [E6].
